title: The 1994 F-150's 4.9L is the EFI 300 variant
The 4.9L takes SAE 5W-30 oil meeting Ford spec ESE-M2C153-E
Change the engine oil and filter every 6 months or 5,000 miles under normal service
A charge light that stays on points to the regulator or stator circuit, not always a dead alternator
The charging system works through three circuits: A (sense), B+ (output), and S (feedback)
The clutch pedal position switch is the start interlock on a manual F-150
Engine coolant service interval is 4 years or 50,000 miles
The 1994 F-150 uses a permanent-magnet gear-reduction starter
A failed throttle-body-to-manifold gasket is a known vacuum-leak cause of rough idle on the 4.9L
The Ford 300 inline-six firing order is 1-5-3-6-2-4
The Ford 300 makes peak torque at low RPM by design
Unplugging the IAC while idling tests whether the idle-air circuit is involved
